Meeting header:

Auto Summary (auto-generated): quick SOC 2/ISO posture review; controls mapping requested; discuss SSO + RBAC integration, KMS/encryption details; next steps to share reports and trust center access plus POC for Dedicated VPC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll kick off — uh — quick intro, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Diego our SE and Priya from security.
[00:06] Sofia Patel: Hi, Sofia here, CISO at Elmbridge. Thanks for fitting us in. We're getting auditors prepped so wanted to walk the posture and map gaps.
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: Great, yeah we put together the controls map, and the trust center link, we'll share the reports too. Quick note — some of the product names in our deck might be munged by the transcriber so apologies in advance.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: We're mostly concerned about storage of PHI-adjacent logs, encryption at rest, KMS usage, and whether audit logs meet our 7 year retention for certain flows.
[00:29] Priya Nair: Yep, we can talk through retention. Redwood's hosted API defaults to 30 day logs for PII redaction but we have Dedicated/Private options that give you control over retention.
[00:40] Asha Roy: Quick Q — does Redwood's Trust Center have the ISO certs and the SOC 2 Type II report? We need evidence for our auditors.
[00:47] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll grant trust center access. The SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 summary are available; full reports require an NDA for download. We'll send instructions and a link.
[00:55] Noah Kim: And for controls mapping, can you map Redwood controls to our internal control IDs? That's super helpful for our audit tracker.
[01:02] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have a controls mapping template — I'll populate it with sample control IDs for Elmbridge and map to SOC/ISO controls and Redwood internal docs.
[01:12] Sofia Patel: On RBAC and SSO, we run Okta with SAML and SCIM for provisioning. We need to confirm SAML vs OIDC support, SCIM user sync and role -> group mapping. Also want least-privilege defaults.
[01:23] Diego Alvarez: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning; our RBAC model supports roles and resource-level scoping. Quick caveat: some fine-grained resource scoping is only available on Dedicated and Private deployments, hosted tier has workspace-level RBAC.
[01:36] Liam O'Connor: Can you clarify that — like service-level or model-route level? We have workflows that call redis-like caches and need to lock down certain model endpoints.
[01:44] Diego Alvarez: Right, so workspace-level RBAC in hosted, meaning roles govern access to projects/workspaces. Dedicated VPC lets you define role bindings tied to customer-managed identities and network policies; and you can lock down model endpoints and routes.
[01:56] Maya Chen: Worth noting the Dedicated option also gives you customer-managed KMS integration.
[02:00] Asha Roy: Ah that's important. We need to use our HSM/KMS provider for key wrapping. What KMS providers do you integrate with?
[02:07] Priya Nair: We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and can support bring-your-own-key through an HSM in Private deployments. There are also envelope encryption options and we publish the key lifecycle docs in the trust center.
[02:20] Sofia Patel: For audit logs — does Redwood provide immutable append-only logs with tamper evidence or just syslog exports?
[02:27] Diego Alvarez: We provide both. Hosted includes structured audit logs via API and syslog/forwarding. Dedicated/Private can do write-once logs and S3 write-once buckets; we can also provide signed log digests for tamper evidence on request.
[02:40] Noah Kim: How granular are the logs — do they contain full request payloads?
[02:44] Maya Chen: Default hosted logs redact request payloads with PII masking; for Dedicated you can opt-in to capture full payloads but that usually comes with contractual constraints around retention and encryption.
[02:54] Asha Roy: We need to know where data is stored — data residency. Is EU data kept in EU zones for both compute and logs?
[03:02] Priya Nair: Yes, we have region-locked deployments. Hosted supports regional processing in EU/US/APAC; Dedicated/Private gives you complete control over the VPC and storage region; we'll include the region mapping doc.
[03:15] Sofia Patel: Controls mapping: can you map specific ISO/ SOC controls to Redwood features? Our auditors want to see how you address things like A.10 crypto controls and CC6 logical access.
[03:25] Diego Alvarez: We'll map at the control level — e.g., ISO A.10 maps to our encryption at rest + KMS docs; SOC Common Criteria will map to RBAC, SSO, MFA, and audit logging exports. I'll annotate with doc links.
[03:37] Liam O'Connor: One of our compliance folks asked about pentest cadence and vulnerability management — are those in scope of SOC and ISO or separate?
[03:45] Priya Nair: They overlap. Our ISO 27001 scope includes vulnerability management and periodic pentests. SOC report references pen test frequency and a summary; for detailed findings we provide redacted summaries. Full vulnerability program docs are in trust center.
[03:58] Asha Roy: Any known limitations or gotchas with data deletion / right to be forgotten? Our HR data team wants assurances.
[04:05] Diego Alvarez: Hosted has standard deletion within 30 days after the retention window; Dedicated gives you direct control and immediate purge options. For regulatory deletion we support API-driven deletion per dataset and audit trails for deletion events.
[04:18] Sofia Patel: On encryption in transit — TLS, mTLS for service-to-service?
[04:22] Priya Nair: TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit always; mTLS is available for Private/Dedicated for service-to-service. For hosted API we support client TLS and token-based auth; we can discuss mTLS on a case-by-case for enterprise tiers.
[04:36] Noah Kim: For our auditors, they asked for sample of how you map Redwood controls to our control IDs — like an example row.
[04:41] Diego Alvarez: I'll add example rows with control ID mapping and evidence links, e.g., Elmbridge-C-004 -> Redwood-SOC2-CC6 -> link to RBAC doc and screenshot.
[04:53] Liam O'Connor: Another practical — latency & throughput for Dedicated if we colocate in their EU region, since some of our flows are time-sensitive and we need to know token latency for inference.
[05:02] Diego Alvarez: We can run a short POC — measure 99th pct latency with your sequence lengths and concurrency. Dedicated in-region typically achieves single-digit 99th percentiles for our transformer sizes depending on quantization; we'll propose a test matrix.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Okay, maybe we should recap the deliverables — we'll give SOC2 & ISO certs via trust center (NDA required for full reports), Diego to send controls mapping + sample logs, and we'll coordinate a Dedicated VPC POC for latency and RBAC tests.
[05:30] Sofia Patel: Sounds good. Also please confirm the legal process for NDA and how long it takes to get trust center access.
[05:36] Maya Chen: Normally 24-48 hours after the signed NDA, we can provision view-only trust center access. We'll include the NDA template in the materials.
[05:43] Asha Roy: One more — do you have an SLA that covers audit log retention and access? For some of our parties, log availability is critical.
[05:50] Priya Nair: Our enterprise SLA covers availability of API and log export functionality; retention is part of the Dedicated contract where you define retention. We'll include SLA excerpt in the trust center packet.
[05:58] Noah Kim: Can Redwood sign a mutual non-disclosure and a standard BAA if we needed HIPAA coverage?
[06:04] Maya Chen: We have a BAA playbook. For HIPAA/BAA we typically require Dedicated or Private deployments and contractual terms. We'll share the BAA template and the path for execution.
[06:14] Diego Alvarez: Also, small note — our hosted inference retains transients differently; if you anticipate PHI we'll recommend Dedicated or Private for compliance.
[06:21] Liam O'Connor: Makes sense. We'll scope PII/PHI flows and decide which model endpoints go to Dedicated.
[06:28] Sofia Patel: Ok final ask — provide a short one-page checklist for our auditors summarizing where to find evidence in the trust center.
[06:34] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Diego and Priya will co-author a one-pager linking to SOC/ISO evidence, RBAC screenshots, audit log samples, KMS docs, and the controls mapping.
[06:44] Closing / Recap
[06:45] Maya Chen: Recap: 
- Maya send trust center link & SOC2/ISO (NDA for full reports)
- Diego send controls mapping + sample audit logs + schedule POC
- Priya attach KMS and encryption lifecycle docs
- Customer to confirm data residency requirements and POC stake holders

[06:58] Sofia Patel: Thanks everyone, that answers most of our immediate auditor questions — we'll get the NDA turned around and Asha will follow up on specifics.
[07:04] Maya Chen: Great — look out for emails from me and Diego. Appreciate the time.
